q: Which describes what happens when sodium reacts with chlorine to form sodium chloride?
options: Each chlorine atom transfers one electron to a sodium atom
A sodium atom and a chlorine atom share a pair of electrons
Each sodium atom transfers two electrons to a chlorine atom
Each sodium atom transfers one electron to a chlorine atom
explain: Sodium (2,8,1) loses one electron to become Na⁺, and chlorine (2,8,7) gains it to become Cl⁻.

q: In a molecule of chlorine, Cl₂, what is shared between the two atoms?
options: Two pairs of electrons
One electron
Three pairs of electrons
One pair of electrons
explain: Each chlorine atom has 7 outer electrons and needs one more, so they share one pair.

q: A student draws a substance in which every particle is a pair of different atoms joined together, and all the pairs are identical. How should this substance be classified?
options: An element
A compound
A mixture of two elements
A mixture of two compounds
explain: Identical particles each containing different atoms chemically joined represent a compound. An element would have only one kind of atom.

q: How many pairs of electrons are shared between the two nitrogen atoms in N₂?
explain: Each nitrogen atom needs three electrons to complete its outer shell, so a triple bond with three shared pairs forms.

q: How many non-bonding electrons are on each nitrogen atom in a molecule of N₂?
explain: Each nitrogen atom has 5 outer electrons: 3 are in the triple bond, leaving 2 as a non-bonding pair.

q: What is a covalent bond?
options: A transfer of electrons from one atom to another
A shared pair of electrons between two atoms
An attraction between oppositely charged ions
An attraction between positive ions and delocalised electrons
explain: In a covalent bond two atoms share a pair of electrons so that each reaches a noble gas configuration.

q: Which row correctly gives the relative charge and relative mass of the particles?
options: neutron | +1 | 1
electron | −1 | 1
proton | +1 | 1
proton | 0 | 1/1840
explain: A proton has charge +1 and relative mass 1. A neutron is neutral with mass 1; an electron has charge −1 and negligible mass.

q: An element is in Group V and Period 2. What is its electronic configuration?
explain: Period 2 means two occupied shells and Group V means five outer electrons: 2,5 (nitrogen).

q: Chlorine consists of 75% ³⁵Cl and 25% ³⁷Cl. What is the relative atomic mass of chlorine?
What does the word delocalised mean in the term delocalised electrons?
options: Fixed in the shell of one atom
Not fixed to one atom and free to move throughout the structure
Present in the nucleus
Shared in a pair between exactly two atoms
explain: Delocalised electrons belong to the whole lattice, not to any single atom.

q: A neutral atom has a proton number of 19. How many electrons does it have?
explain: A neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons, so 19 protons means 19 electrons.

q: What does the term ductile mean?
options: Can be hammered into thin sheets
Can be melted easily
Can be drawn out into a wire
Can conduct electricity
explain: Ductile describes the ability to be stretched into wires; malleable means able to be hammered into shape.

q: Which statement explains why the formula of silicon(IV) oxide is SiO₂?
options: Each silicon atom is bonded to two oxygen atoms and each oxygen atom to one silicon atom
Silicon ions Si²⁺ combine with oxide ions O²⁻
Each silicon atom is bonded to four oxygen atoms and each oxygen atom is shared between two silicon atoms
Each oxygen atom is bonded to four silicon atoms
explain: Four Si–O bonds per silicon, with each oxygen forming two bonds, gives two oxygen atoms for each silicon atom.

q: A hydrogen atom shares its electron in a covalent bond. How many electrons does it then have in its outer shell?
explain: Hydrogen has one shell, which is full with two electrons, the noble gas configuration of helium.

q: How many pairs of electrons are shared between the two oxygen atoms in an oxygen molecule, O₂?
explain: Each oxygen atom needs two more electrons, so two pairs are shared, forming a double bond.

q: Why does solid sodium chloride not conduct electricity?
options: It contains no ions
Its ions are held in fixed positions in the lattice and cannot move
Its electrons are delocalised but cannot move
Its ions are too small to carry charge
explain: Conduction needs charged particles that are free to move; ions in the solid lattice only vibrate in place.

q: A magnesium atom has two outer electrons. In solid magnesium, what happens to these electrons?
options: They are transferred to chlorine atoms
They stay fixed on each magnesium atom
They become delocalised and move through the lattice of Mg²⁺ ions
They are shared in pairs between two atoms
explain: Each atom releases its outer electrons into the shared sea, leaving Mg²⁺ ions in the lattice.

q: Which pair of properties do both diamond and silicon(IV) oxide have?
options: Low melting point and conduct electricity
Very high melting point and do not conduct electricity
Very high melting point and conduct electricity
Low melting point and do not conduct electricity
explain: Both are giant covalent structures with strong bonds and no mobile charged particles.

q: An atom has the electronic configuration 2,8,6. How many protons does it have in its nucleus?
explain: A neutral atom has equal protons and electrons: 2 + 8 + 6 = 16 (sulfur).

q: What is the electronic configuration of an oxide ion, O²⁻ (oxygen has proton number 8)?
explain: The oxygen atom (2,6) gains two electrons, giving 10 electrons arranged 2,8.

q: Why do simple molecular substances not conduct electricity?
options: They contain strong covalent bonds
They contain positive ions fixed in a lattice
They contain no ions or free electrons to carry the charge
They have low melting points
explain: Molecules are uncharged and have no mobile charged particles, so no current can flow.

q: Which diagram description represents a metal?
options: A regular arrangement of alternating positive and negative ions
Pairs of atoms each joined by a shared pair of electrons
A regular arrangement of positive ions surrounded by a sea of free electrons
Layers of atoms with weak forces between the layers
explain: Metals have lattices of positive ions in a sea of electrons; the second option is an ionic lattice and the third a molecule.

q: Which type of element atoms tend to form positive ions?
options: Non-metals
Noble gases
Metals
Halogens
explain: Metal atoms lose their outer electrons to form positive ions; non-metals usually gain electrons.

q: Which statement about the electrons in a metal is correct?
options: The electrons are only attracted to the ion they came from
The electrons are repelled by all the positive ions
The electrons are shared in fixed pairs between two ions
The delocalised electrons are attracted to all of the positive ions in the lattice
explain: The sea of electrons is attracted to many ions at once, which holds the lattice together and allows movement without breaking it.

q: Which is the formula of calcium chloride?
options: CaCl
Ca₂Cl
CaCl₂
Ca₂Cl₂
explain: Ca²⁺ needs two Cl⁻ ions to balance charge: one calcium atom loses two electrons and each of two chlorine atoms gains one.

q: Diamond and graphite are both forms of which element?
options: Silicon
Sulfur
Carbon
Lead
explain: Diamond and graphite are two structures made of carbon atoms only.

q: Which particles are present in a metal lattice?
options: Positive ions and negative ions
Neutral atoms and molecules
Positive ions and delocalised electrons
Negative ions and delocalised electrons
explain: A metal consists of positive metal ions in a regular arrangement with a sea of electrons around them.

q: In a molecule of hydrogen chloride, HCl, how many non-bonding pairs of electrons are in the outer shell of the chlorine atom?
explain: Chlorine has 7 outer electrons: one is shared with hydrogen and the other 6 form 3 non-bonding pairs.

q: Why does solid copper conduct electricity but solid sodium chloride does not?
options: Copper has mobile ions in the solid, but sodium chloride has none
Copper has molecules but sodium chloride has a lattice
Sodium chloride has delocalised electrons that cannot move
Copper has delocalised electrons that can move, but sodium chloride's ions are fixed
explain: Metals have mobile electrons even when solid, whereas ionic solids have charged particles that cannot move.

q: Which statement describes the structure of an ionic compound such as sodium chloride?
options: Separate molecules of NaCl held by weak forces
A giant lattice of alternating positive and negative ions in a regular arrangement
A giant lattice of positive ions in a sea of electrons
Pairs of atoms joined by shared electrons
explain: Ionic compounds form a regular three-dimensional lattice in which each ion is surrounded by ions of opposite charge.
